newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork belly calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork belly calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.150 cent a lb lower to 0.200 higher while pork belly futures indications ranged from 0.200 cent lower to 0.100 higher, livestock analysts said.
A few analysts look for pressure in hog futures on ideas of weaker cash hog prices as packers likely have adequate hogs to meet slaughter needs.

However, other analysts look for renewed strength to develop as poor weather starts to hamper hog movement in the western Corn Belt. Packer margins also improved as pork cutout values moved up to one-month highs.

Grade two estimated gross pork cutout value rose to $77.75 per cwt, the highest level since October 13. Part of the advance in cutout values came from stronger cash belly prices, which rose to as much as $71 Monday. The price was the highest since October 8.
The stronger cash belly market, continued light slaughter and an oversold futures condition could stimulate support in belly futures early, some analysts said.
However, others look for further technical selling after futures ran into heavy resistance on the charts under 80 cents Monday and fell back sharply.
Trade may also be uneven ahead of the weekly CME out-of-town pork belly report, they added.

Estimates on the out-of-town report ranged from in 1.25 million to 2.5 million lbs last week versus an in-movement of 2.83 million last week and an in-movement of 4.191 million last year during the corresponding week.
